statement.label: Statement
paragraphs: Over the past three years, I have been working hard to address the issues that residents of District 4 asked me to prioritize: ensuring our criminal and civil legal systems are operating effectively and fairly so we can enhance community safety; stabilizing and strengthening our homelessness response system so we can reduce the number of people living unhoused in our region; protecting our public health clinics and investing in our county hospital, Harborview Medical Center, so we can preserve access to health care; improving the safety and reliability of our Metro transit system; and much more.

My team and I have been focused on making progress on these complex issues, but I know much more work remains to be done and I remain committed to these priorities. I also recognize that the reality for many in our community today is very different from what it was in 2023 when I first ran for this office. At the time, a second Trump Administration was a possibility. Today, it’s a reality that is threatening the safety and well-being of so many, especially our immigrant and transgender neighbors.

Particularly at a time like this, I believe it is crucial to have leaders in state and local government who will be uncompromising in defending and advancing our community’s values in the face of an increasingly chaotic and authoritarian federal administration, while also continuing to pursue progressive policies that will improve the lives of our residents.
For these reasons, I am asking you, my neighbors in District 4, to give me the opportunity to continue representing you on the King County Council.

Endorsed by Governor Bob Ferguson; Attorney General Nick Brown; Representative Pramila Jayapal; King County Executive Girmay Zahilay; King County Democrats; state and local elected leaders; labor; and social and environmental justice organizations.

statement.label: Statement
paragraphs: I’m proud to have served as a regional leader, delivering results for East King County and communities across our region. Throughout my time on the King County Council, I’ve brought people together to tackle our biggest challenges with practical solutions and a focus on getting things done.

Representing you, I’ve led efforts to expand affordable housing, chairing the Regional Affordable Housing Committee and working with cities, housing providers, labor, business, and community organizations to plan for more than 200,000 new affordable homes across King County. I’ve championed transit-oriented development to create thousands of affordable homes near light rail, helped implement Health through Housing, secured stable funding for arts and culture through Doors Open, and continued leading the expansion of our regional transit system, including opening light rail across the I-90 bridge to the Eastside. I’ve also worked to strengthen homelessness and behavioral health services, improve public safety, preserve parks and open space, protect reproductive freedom, defend immigrant communities, and invest in programs that support children, families, and workers.

As Council Chair during the COVID-19 pandemic, I led the Council’s response to keep county government open, delivering critical assistance to workers, renters, small businesses, and vulnerable residents. I sponsored the charter amendment moving county elections to even-numbered years so a much larger and more diverse electorate selects their local government representatives.

There is still more work to do. I will continue expanding affordable housing, improving public health and safety through smart investments with accountability, completing our regional transit network, protecting our environment, supporting small businesses and working families, and ensuring King County delivers effective, accountable government that reflects the values of the people it serves. It would be an honor to earn your vote once again.

paragraphs: Masters in Public Administration, focus in health policy, Evergreen State College; BA, University of Washington

statement.label: Occupation
paragraphs: County Councilmember; labor champion, children’s advocate, public health policy leader

statement.label: Statement
paragraphs: I’m running for re-election to the County Council to continue building a healthier, safer, more affordable King County where working families can thrive. At a time when costs are rising and many neighbors are struggling to stay housed, maintain access to care, and make ends meet - we need bold leadership that delivers real results for our communities.

I’ve spent my career fighting for workers, kiddos, and healthy communities. At the Children’s Alliance and the Washington State Labor Council, I helped win paid sick leave, minimum wage increases, and stronger protections for workers and immigrants. On the Seattle City Council and now at King County, I’ve built coalitions to expand affordable housing, strengthen worker protections, invest in behavioral health, and support small businesses and community safety.

At King County, I’ve worked to increase investments in affordable and supportive housing, improve behavioral health services, protect immigrant and refugee communities, and strengthen our public health infrastructure. I’ve also championed investments in transit, childcare, and workforce development to help families stay and succeed in our region.

My priorities remain expanding affordable housing and preventing displacement; improving community safety through behavioral health and gun violence prevention; and investing in working families with accessible transit, childcare, healthcare, and union job opportunities.

As a judge I will hear both sides in full and hold the prosecution and the defense to the same standard. Accountability should fit the offense and leave the person better able to stay out of court.
I am asking for your vote.

paragraphs: Judge Damon Shadid has dedicated his time at the Seattle Municipal Court trying to find better ways of approaching criminal justice. He has a deep understanding that the criminal legal system should have two primary and complementary objectives: keep the community safe and help people obtain the services they need to exit the criminal legal system.

With these objectives in mind, Judge Shadid’s colleagues on the court have tapped him to work with the Seattle City Attorney and the Department of Public Defense to form a new “Connection Court” which is being built on the foundation of Judge Shadid’s work in the former Community Court. Connection Court gives participants the option of being quickly connected with services in the community to address the underlying causes of their crimes.

Judge Shadid has also been instrumental in re-building the Seattle Mental Health Court, where he presided for 4 years. He was able to work with the City Attorney’s Office and the Department of Public Defense to improve the Mental Health Court and to encourage more individuals with mental health barriers get the vital services they need.

Finally, Judge Shadid started the “Consolidated Calendar.” This court allows individuals who have case workers in the community to come to one calendar each week in order to help their clients receive services and exit from the criminal legal system.

But the work is not done. Seattle faces profound challenges stemming from a lack of vital services like housing, substance abuse treatment and mental health treatment which cause public safety issues in our community. Judge Shadid believes that the Municipal Court should play a central role in improving access to these services, and will continue to work hard every day to ensure that all people are treated with fairness and compassion.
